summary: Nikolai Solmsdorf is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, also studying under Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2013.

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford in 2010 under Alexis Sanderson. In 2020, she held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Oxford and Yale. He taught at Nottingham, Birmingham, and Lancaster University, and was J. F. Rowny Professor of Comparative Religions at UC Santa Barbara (attested 1993–2001).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter Bisschop in 2015. He later held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2019) and as a postdoctoral researcher at Leiden University (attested 2021).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from Cambridge. He served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1934–1940) and rose to Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950) at the Archaeological Survey of India.

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of History at Krishnath College and Centenary Professor of International Relations at the University of Calcutta.
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford in 2003 under Richard Gombrich. She has held a post as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo (~1974–1994), Taisho University (~1994–2004), and the Open University of Japan.
Noboru Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an attested post at the University of Tokyo in 1990 and was an attested professor at Mejiro University in 2015.

Nobuchiyo Kotani (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama. He served as a professor at Otani University (~1988–2015) and president of Otani University Junior College (~2001–2007).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and later as an assistant professor at Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota (born 1969) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1988–1999). He was a Research Fellow at the University of Tokyo (~1999–2001) and joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2007.
Nobukatsu Komai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a research student at Taisho University and held a position as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpoin (attested 2014).

Tensho Miyazaki (born 1978) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University (~2010–2013), Tokyo University of Agriculture (attested 2015), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2015).

Nobumi Iyanaga (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a lecturer at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and held a research contract at the École française d'Extrême-Orient's Tokyo Centre from 2008 to 2014.

Nobunaga Takasa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a post as an assistant professor at National Institute of Technology, Sendai College (attested 1991) and as a researcher at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Nobuo Otsuka (born 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University (~1983–1988), where he later served as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (born 1960) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, he held faculty posts at several junior colleges, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and Waseda University (~2015).
